newsitem.title: DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF CONGO: Three demonstrators killed by troops in Kinshasa.
newsitem.headline: Three demonstrators killed by troops in Kinshasa.

text.p: Three people were shot dead by soldiers in Kinshasa on Friday during a protest by about 1,000 opposition activists at President Laurent Kabila's banning of political activity, witnesses said.

The soldiers opened fire after the demonstrators from the radical PALU party loyal to the memory of nationalist independence leader Patrice Lumumba tried to regroup after being dispersed by police, witnesses added.
Witnesses also reported five injured among the demonstrators, who had been marching from the central railway station to the presidency of Kabila's renamed Democratic Republic of the Congo.
Police fired into the air in an attempt to disperse the crowd in front of the presidency, causing the marchers to flee in panic and then regroup near the foreign ministry, where soldiers opened fire.

Kabila, whose forces toppled veteran dictator Mobutu Sese Seko in May, has banned all protest marches by opposition parties. He has given himself wide-ranging powers as president. Elections are planned in 1999.
Most opposition protests to date have featured supporters or allies of veteran Mobutu opponent Etienne Tshisekedi, the main political opposition leader in the former Zaire.
